# Exercises for Part III {.unnumbered #sec-exercises-water}

These exercises collect Part III's hands-on work in order, one per checkpoint, as Part II's did. Start
the assistant in `~/water-quality/`, next to `~/quarto-workshop/`. The water checkpoints hold sources
only, so each catch-up also copies `examples/water/data/` into your folder if `data/` is missing. From
Exercise III.4 on, the normal route copies each block's finished `scripts/analysis.py`; the prompts that
write the analysis yourself are optional. @sec-checkpoints has the whole table.

## Exercise III.1: rules, environment and a first look {.unnumbered}

From @sec-water-question and @sec-explore. Copy the data, write `AGENTS.md` from the data's README,
create the uv environment, and build `explore.qmd`.

::: done
`explore.html` shows missing values by zone and IRCA by band, zone and year for 2010–2023.
:::

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/checkpoints/05-water-explore/README.md
```
:::

## Exercise III.6: report, slides and e-book {.unnumbered}

From @sec-publish-many. Build `report.qmd` (HTML, Word, Typst PDF), `slides.qmd` (Reveal.js and
PowerPoint) and, optionally, the report's EPUB.

::: done
`report.docx` and `report.pdf` open with the heatmap, the outcomes and the within-cluster figure;
`slides.html` and `slides.pptx` both have six slides; and, if you made it, `report.epub` opens with the
three figures and the sources.
:::

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/checkpoints/10-water-report/README.md
```
:::

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/checkpoints/11-water-slides/README.md
```
:::

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/checkpoints/12-water-epub/README.md
```
:::

Use the catch-up for the last step you completed: 10 after the report, 11 after the slides, 12 after the
optional e-book.

## Exercise III.7: the website, published {.unnumbered}

From @sec-water-website and @sec-water-ship. Make the folder a website with a blog post titled with the real
k, put it on GitHub, and publish it with an interactive `uv run quarto publish gh-pages`.

::: done
`https://<your-github-username>.github.io/water-quality/` opens, and its home page lists one post whose title
states the real k.
:::

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/checkpoints/13-water-website/README.md
```
:::

## Exercise III.8: change an input, explain the rebuild {.unnumbered}

From @sec-water-change, with no prompt supplied. Change `MAX_MISSING = 2` to `1` in
`scripts/analysis.py`, predict which outputs change, rebuild, explain, and undo with
`git restore scripts/analysis.py`.

::: done
you can name the outputs that changed, the ones that did not, and the mechanism that links them
(`pre-render`, `outputs/`, `freeze: false`). The model answer is in @sec-checkpoints.
:::

## Going further {.unnumbered}

1. **Optional pieces.** Build the dashboard and the white paper (@sec-water-dashboard); the finished project,
   `examples/water/`, is their checkpoint:

   ::: catchup
   ```default
   Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/examples/water/README.md
   ```
   :::

2. **Change the seed.** Repeat Exercise III.8 with `SEED` instead of `MAX_MISSING`. Clusters are numbered by
   their centre's IRCA, so the names and colours should stay; check whether anything else moves, and why
   very little does (@sec-choose-k, on stability).
3. **Freeze it.** Switch the site to `freeze: auto`, change `MAX_MISSING`, render, and find a page that kept
   its old numbers. Then write the invalidation rule into the project's `AGENTS.md`, apply it, and undo both
   changes.
4. **The challenges** in @sec-water-stretch: moves between kinds as a Sankey diagram, positive deviants, and
   other clustering methods.
